_readme: Parts map for tools/gen_jlc_bom_cpl.py, and the source of the LCSC field gen_spec.py
stamps onto every symbol -- edit a number HERE and it flows into the schematic.
KEY IS 'value|footprint' EXACTLY AS IT APPEARS ON THE BOARD -- that is what the BOM
script looks up. Keyed by bare value it silently matches NOTHING and every line comes
out unsourced. Keys are generated from spec.json, not typed.
The composite key is also the package guard, and it earned its keep: the cheapest BASIC
8MHz crystal (C12674) is HC-49S-SMD and would not have fitted the 5032 lands here.
PREFER JLC 'basic' PARTS EVEN WHEN DEARER. At qty 1 the per-unique-extended-part fee is
a fixed cost, so with ~48 lines those fees dominate the build. 74HC595: the basic SOIC-16
is $0.171 against $0.044 for the cheapest extended SOP-16 - 39 cents more across 3 chips,
against a per-part fee many times that.
Four SUBSTITUTIONS against what the design first called for, all folded back into
gen_spec.py so the schematic agrees: AMS1117-3.3 for LD1117S33 (basic), M95640 for
25LC640 (half the price, better stocked), 20pF for 12pF crystal load caps (the 12pF was
simply wrong for a 12.5pF crystal - see DESIGN.md), and a 60V PPTC over a 30V one.
STATUS: every assembled line sourced. The four nulls are 2.54mm headers fitted by hand,
excluded from BOM and CPL via exclude_refs.
